title: Sum of Left Leaves
summary: Calculate the total sum of all nodes that are left children and have no children in a given binary tree.
statement: Calculate the total sum of all nodes that are left children and have no children in a given binary tree.
constraints: A left leaf has no children and is its parent's left child. The root itself is never a left leaf.

hints: Being a left child and being a leaf are separate requirements.
Carry a flag indicating whether each visited node came from a left edge.
Add a value only when the flag is true and both children are absent; push children with their corresponding flags.
Start the root with a false flag. The same state can be passed through recursion.
editorial: Traverse the tree with pairs of a node and a left-child flag. A node contributes precisely when its flag is true and it has no children. Each left child gets a true flag; each right child gets false. The root starts false. The explicit stack avoids recursion limits on a 1000-node chain, while expressing the same state that a recursive solution would pass.
